title: TimeLens batching recommendation orchestrator and safe shadow-apply
creator: Maya Patel
description: Build TimeLens: a continuous batching recommendation orchestrator that profiles request streams with a time-decayed window, extracts workload signatures, and synthesizes conservative batching parameters plus KV/prefix cache hints. TimeLens produces per-route recommendations (target_batch_size, microbatch_timeout_ms, kv_prefix_cache_lifetime) and an automated safe shadow-apply harness that validates candidate configs against latency SLOs, tail-p99 regressions, and quality-preservation heuristics before gradual production rollout. Key design constraints: 1) recommendations must be explainable (rule provenance + telemetry anchors), 2) safety-first: reject any config that increases 95th-99th percentile latency beyond configured thresholds or reduces prompt-level quality score by >1% for tracked evals, 3) accept workload drift and continuous annealing (parameters should adapt but require safety checkpoints and human-review triggers).
acceptance_criteria: TimeLens collects and stores 30-day time-decayed workload summaries per route (arrival rate distribution, median tokens, token variance, KV-hit ratio) in telemetry store
Recommendation API returns target_batch_size and microbatch_timeout_ms with rationale string and confidence score for any route sampled in the last 24 hours
Shadow-apply harness can run candidate config against 0.5% shadow traffic or locally replayed traces and emit a safety verdict (PASS/FAIL) based on latency, cost delta, and quality regressions
Automated canary rollout supports staged apply (5% -> 25% -> 100%) with automatic rollback on regression thresholds and emits rollback reason in the console
End-to-end integration tests cover: offline replay evaluation (+/-10% cost accuracy), shadow-apply verdict, and rollback workflow
Dashboard panel in Console (per-route) shows previous vs recommended params, expected cost reduction estimate, and safety signals
comments: 2026-02-18 Maya Patel: Kickoff — scoped MVP: profiler + recommender + simple shadow-apply. Focus on routes with >5 RPS and median tokens >64 to prioritize ROI.

2026-02-24 Julian Kim: Prototype profiler implemented. Uses exponential time decay (alpha=0.1) to weight recent traffic. Verified against stored traces for three customer routes — median batchable window identified correctly.

2026-03-02 SRE review (R. Singh): Raised concerns about shadow-apply overhead on tail latency for busy nodes. Action: isolate shadow traffic to spare infer nodes or replay locally to avoid interference.
2026-03-03 Design feedback (L. Nguyen): Recommendation UI should show a short human-readable rationale and link to the trace sample that generated the recommendation. Added to ACs.

2026-03-05 Experiment update: Run with two candidate heuristics: 'quantile-aware' (targets p90 latency constraint) and 'cost-first' (maximizes expected token coalescing). Initial results: quantile-aware kept p95 stable; cost-first gave 12% cost savings but caused p99 spikes on bursty routes — will tune conservatism.

2026-03-08 Infra (K. Alvarez): Added a lightweight replay runner on staging that can feed stored traces to a candidate cluster; avoids hitting prod nodes. Works for 80% of routes; remaining require live shadowing.

2026-03-10 Julian Kim: Implemented safety verdict logic: combine latency SLO checks (p95/p99), cost delta prediction, and eval-based quality regression check. Default thresholds: p95 increase >5ms OR p99 increase >10ms OR eval quality drop >1% => FAIL.

2026-03-10 Maya Patel: Next: integrate the recommendation API with Console and add 'explain' field that captures top-3 contributing signals (e.g., high token variance, KV-hit low, steady arrival rate).
